accuracy.evidence: Definitions follow CCSS RL.K.3 and RL.1.3 and common story grammar usage (Stein and Glenn 1979): characters are who acts, the setting is place and time, events are what happens. Each tale detail was checked against standard retellings: Goldilocks goes into the bears' house in the woods, eats Baby Bear's porridge and runs home; in The Gingerbread Man an old woman bakes him, a cow is among those who chase him in the common English versions, and a fox carries him over the river; in The Three Little Pigs the wolf blows down the straw and stick houses but not the brick one; in The Enormous Turnip a grandfather, grandmother, dog, cat and mouse pull it up (the Tolstoy version adds a granddaughter; the lab card lists the helpers named in the short retelling it shows). Setting phrases are labelled where or when consistently.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the confusions teachers report for RL.K.3 and RL.1.3 and in story-grammar teaching guides (Reading Rockets story map guidance; Stein and Glenn): setting taken as place only (one morning in step 1, one night prediction, challenge 'place' and p3), characters must be people or any object counts (Gingerbread Man prediction, oven and river feedback, m2, m9, challenge 'thing'), mixing an event with a character or setting (sort feedback, m4, challenge 'swap'), and retelling every detail or only the ending (key events step, m6, challenge 'detail' and 'short').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagsmap is about naming story elements: a three-basket sort of Goldilocks cards into characters, setting and events, a who-counts-as-a-character board where a biscuit counts and an oven and a river do not, tap-the-clue story openings that fill Where and When boxes, a key-event versus small-detail filter for The Three Little Pigs, and a four-part story map for The Enormous Turnip with off-story decoys. flagaloud is about listening and answering from the text, and flagtale is about ordering a story with time words; neither sorts element types, filters key events from details or builds a story map. lab_distinct gate passes under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds each rule by doing: wrong baskets explain what makes a card a character, a setting or an event (and that one morning is a when), the oven and river refuse with the reason, setting clue words drop into Where and When as they are found, details are greyed out with 'take it out and the story still works', and the city and dragon cards are refused because they are not in the story.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: 'No, characters are people' for the Gingerbread Man (he is accepted as a character), 'What happens' for 'One night' (it lands in the When box), and 'Yes, it is in the story' for the wolf's big ears (it is rejected as a small detail).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions; each wrong option carries one of five distinct messages that name the slip: a who given as the setting, an object or place taken for a character, a small detail taken for a key event, an event swapped with a character or setting, and a retelling with only the ending. Answer order rotates between questions.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences built on well-known tales and plain words (who, where, when, what happens); the adult text names CCSS RL.K.3, RL.1.3, RL.K.2 and RL.1.2, the Year 1 programme of study wording and the key vocabulary. Card texts are short phrases; the lab uses the young layout. validate_lessons readability passes.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Each kid paragraph adds a different element: the three parts, what makes a character, setting as where and when, key events and retelling. Items cover characters (p1, p4, m3, m7, m9), setting (p2, p3, m1, m2, m8), events (p5, m4), retelling (m6) and story maps (m5).

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 light and dark, 360 px Android light and dark and desktop dark screenshots of every step at the start and after Show me. On phones the canvas is taller and the pig and turnip cards use two columns so card text stays at 10 px or more; baskets keep their names readable in both themes; clue chips wrap to a second line instead of clipping. Real drags into baskets and onto the story map were tested on desktop and iPhone 13.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin: pick a card then a basket, one button per Gingerbread Man picture, one per clue phrase, one per pig card, and pick a card then a map part. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the reason a card does or does not fit. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
